steps.description: This is a pure ML/math experiment testing the algebraic variety hypothesis on solution space rigidity using small feedforward networks. We will: (1) construct a polynomial constraint system of degree 3 in R^4 with a low-dimensional algebraic solution set (rigid) vs. a higher-dimensional one (fat); (2) sample w constraint points from each manifold; (3) train small feedforward networks (varying hidden width) to satisfy all w constraints with max absolute error ≤ 1e-3 on a held-out set; (4) measure N_c(w) = minimum width achieving zero violation; (5) compare N_c(w) trends: rigid should show small, w-independent N_c; fat should show N_c growing with w or exceeding scan limit. We'll implement custom PyTorch training with Adam optimizer, batch size 64, max 2000 epochs, and early stopping. Output: N_c(w) table, training/validation error curves, and rigidity classification.
